def: A number whose value depends on the outcome of a chance process, such as the sum of two dice or the next token id.
A curve whose area over an interval is the probability that a continuous variable lands in it; its height is probability per unit, so it can exceed 1.
The probability-weighted average of a random variable's values, which is linear even for dependent variables.
The expected squared distance from the mean, measuring spread; it adds for independent variables.
The standard deviation of an estimate such as a sample mean, equal to sigma divided by the square root of n.
The average of many independent draws converges to the expectation of the distribution they come from.
The average of many independent draws with finite variance becomes approximately Gaussian, whatever the shape of the original distribution.
The probability of one event given that another is known to have happened, P(A | B) = P(A, B) / P(B).
A joint probability written as a product of each variable given all earlier ones, the identity behind autoregressive language models.
The identity P(H | E) = P(E | H) P(H) / P(E) that turns a likelihood and a prior into a posterior.
The prior is belief about a hypothesis before seeing evidence; the posterior is the updated belief afterwards.
Drawing from any distribution by feeding a uniform random number through the inverse of its cumulative distribution function.
Estimating an expectation by averaging a function over random samples, with error shrinking as one over the square root of the sample count.
Estimating an expectation under one distribution using samples from another, each re-weighted by the ratio of the two densities.
A divisor applied to logits before the softmax: below 1 sharpens the distribution toward the largest logit, above 1 flattens it.
